# PROBLEM DESCRIPTION

# "Layout/Easy Layout (Responsive)" in FullControlTest

The goal is to add a new page to FullControlTest to demo how easy layout could work with responsive layout. Before starting the task there is two sub task needs to do:

1) Some place uses "eazy" instead of "easy", this is incorrect. Please fix FullControlTest.

2) I would like a horizontal layout of the tab control in `Layout` tab to list tab headers vertically. So you have to add a new `VerticalTabTemplate.xml` to store that new control template. It should work with color theme in the `DarkSkin` in use, you can verify that by changing the color theme and go back to this page, see if color actually changes. And instead using `<Tab/>` you are going to switch to `<RibbonTab/>` for this particular tab, so that you will get the `BeforeHeaders` and `AfterHeaders` properties. In the control template, `BeforeHeaders` maps to the space above vertical tab headers, and `AfterHeaders` maps to all space below vertical tab headers. The new `Easy Layout (Responsive)` is not a tab page, you are going to put a button instead to the `AfterHeaders`, making sure that the button has a gap of 5 pixels between the last tab header. The gap should be implemented in the button's layout by `AlignmentToParent="left:0 top:5 right:0 bottom:-1"`, the control template does not insert gaps between `BeforeHeaders` -- tab headers -- `AfterHeaders`.

Now you are going to implmenet the new page as a window, create `EasyLayoutResponsiveWindow.xml` and `EasyLayoutResponsiveTemplates.xml` to store that window. Clicking `Easy Layout (Responsive)` opens it as a model window.

The reason to make a new window is that, `FullControlTest`'s smallest size is too big, it is not possible to shink it small enough to trigger the responsive layout we expect to see. So when opening this new window, set its client size to `x:240 y:320` and make it resizable. By changing the size of the window you can trigger the responsive layout, therefore you can test if it re-layout content expectedly.

## Content of the New Test Window

The main layout will be implemented with `ez:Layout`:

```plaintext
+--------------------------+
| Here is responsive       |
| Buttons below are        |
|   not included           |
+--------------------------+
|            | OK | Cancel |
+--------------------------+
```

The `OK` and `Cancel` button doing the same thing to close the window.

The content will be mainly copied from `../Release/Tutorial/GacUI_Layout/Responsive2` which means:
- The #1 layout will be menu + scrollable content
- The #2 layout will be icon options + scrollable content
- The #3 layout will be icon-name options + scrollable content

But instead of making scrollable content looks like some big icons, you are going to make it like a list organized list item vertically. Use a real list control with responsive list item template. `ResponsiveGroup` will be a good parent for storing the list control, as all list item will "response" at the same time, so that to create the #0 layout:
- In #0 layout, all list items will be just movie names
- In #1..#3 layout, all list items will be organized in an 2x2 table like:
  - The left side will be the movie icon picture
  - The right side will be the movie title, followed by the author.

But this time we are demoing `<ez:Layout>`, so even though the `Responsive2` is using raw compositions, we should use `<ez:Layout>` everywhere appropriately.
Organize the layout to keep it easy to understand.

## File Organization

`EasyLayoutResponsiveTemplates.xml` stores all templates used in this window.
`EasyLayoutResponsiveWindow.xml` stores the window, data structure for the movie list. Initialization of account list and movie list could be done in a workflow function and called in the window's constructor. Everything should be done in the xml file, no C++ should be involved to prepare the data.
All new XML files in FullControlTest should be indexed in `GacUI_Compiler` project, also scan if any xml files are missing in other test apps and skins.
All changes should reflect to `.github/Jobs/DebugRemoteProtocolSop.md` if affected, keep unaffected content unchanged. Testing job should be able to follow `DebugRemoteProtocolSop.md` and see if the color theme for the tab and responsive layout is working.

## No.2 Window-owned selection and state-free virtual responsive lists

This extends No.1 with the requested improvements. Source inspection confirms the following before implementation:

- `ez:Layout.Border` defaults to true and adds outside spacing rather than a painted border. Set the main layout to false. A surrounding `SharedSizeRoot` can synchronize two footer `SharedSizeItem` wrappers without changing descriptor ownership.
- `GuiListItemTemplate.Index` is supplied by the list. The account model does not need its own index. Replace the scrollable repeat stack with a real bindable text list and render its list-owned selection normally.
- The concrete list API is `SelectedItemIndex` (read-only) plus `SetSelected`, rather than a writable `SelectedIndex`. `SelectionChanged` fires after updating selection and carries no previous index. Synchronize the eight account `Selected` flags in the window's handler from `GetSelected(i)`, covering mouse, keyboard and UIA without another retained selection variable. Menu actions are attached by the window and select the corresponding list item; templates only render names and selected-image bindings.
- Responsive groups do find item views across a list viewport, so the width-forwarding empty view remains useful for both lists. However, `<GacUI repo>/Source/GraphicsComposition/GuiGraphicsResponsiveComposition.cpp` only registers newly inserted responsive children and computes the maximum level; it does not initialize their level. Virtual rows start rich, and their width is hidden by the viewport. Therefore the empty view alone is insufficient after scrolling at an unchanged narrow width. Window-owned item factories will initialize each new row's named responsive view from the actual width view before the list attaches it. This removes `EasyResponsiveState` and both model state references without changing library behavior or retaining a duplicate level.
- Use natural-size, centered account images and enlarge movie images from 64 to 96 pixels. Keep title and director tracks within the image height. Move all responsive images into a linked `<GacUI repo>/Test/Resources/App/FullControlTest/ResponsiveImages/Images.xml`, including the requested copied selection arrow.
- Use the first 24 films from the [BFI Sight and Sound 2022 critics' poll](https://www.bfi.org.uk/sight-and-sound/greatest-films-all-time), including the two entries tied at rank 21. These are sample data from a named ranking, not an objective universal best list. Publisher accounts use Penguin Random House, HarperCollins, Simon & Schuster, Hachette Book Group, Macmillan Publishers, Scholastic, Bloomsbury and Oxford University Press; the two lists remain unrelated.

The DOM records the null descriptor while the native element can retain the old arrow. The first focused C++ UIA run exposed another shared-library defect: a fitting movie list has no horizontal scrollbar in Controls, yet ScrollPattern reports it scrollable with a 10-percent view. `GuiScrollView::AdjustView` disables a fitting axis while retaining its previous/default scrollbar range. The Windows UIA provider incorrectly reads that retained range without checking the scrollbar's own Enabled state. Extend the proposal with one common axis-scrollability predicate using Enabled and a positive range; use it for pattern getters, direct properties and both scrolling actions. A fitting axis must report false, a 100-percent view and NoScroll, as specified by [Microsoft's Scroll contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winauto/uiauto-implementingscroll). Parent control enablement remains independent. Validate both requested axes before mutating either, and observe the scrollbar's EnabledChanged event so containing-view property snapshots stay current. Shared UIA regressions will compare direct properties with pattern values, verify fitting-axis values through resize transitions, and ensure rejected two-axis requests preserve both positions.

### CONFIRMED

No.2 is the selected final refinement of No.1. It keeps the original vertical-tab/modal demonstration and replaces duplicated selection/layout state with the actual account-list selection and responsive width views. Both lists use real virtualized controls. Templates only render data; the window attaches menu actions and synchronizes each account's local `Selected` flag. `EasyResponsiveAccount.Index` and the complete `EasyResponsiveState` are removed.

The empty-view technique works across both list viewports, with one necessary addition: newly realized item templates must inherit the width view's current level before being attached to the responsive group. Without that initialization, a newly realized rich row can raise the group level during narrow scrolling. The window-owned factories solve that case without another retained level variable. Forward/reverse scrolling in all appearances and both C++ implementations, plus Workflow execution and native remote rendering, verify this behavior.

The requested visual/resource changes are complete: images are linked through their own folder resource, the outer easy layout has no border spacing, a surrounding shared-size root equalizes both footer buttons, account images stay centered at their natural 32-pixel size, movie images measure 96 pixels, the sample uses 24 named films/directors and eight unrelated publishers, and exactly one selected menu entry shows the copied green arrow. The native renderer now clears an image when its protocol ID becomes null; its unit regression verifies the real image element rather than only the descriptor.
